hook: A U.S. military aircrew in the Arabian Gulf in 2020 locked onto a UAP with a weapons-quality targeting track and visually identified it via infrared sensor, describing it as balloon-like and consistent with a previously reported UAP from the 48th Fighter Wing.
why_it_matters: This report is notable because the crew achieved a 'weapons quality 1 track' on the object, meaning it was tracked with sufficient fidelity to generate a fire-control solution — a higher standard of sensor confirmation than a casual sighting. The explicit cross-reference to a prior 48FW report suggests military units were accumulating a pattern-of-life on balloon-like UAP in different theaters, which has implications for how the military was categorizing and comparing recurring UAP encounters.

key_findings.finding: The UAP was described as balloon-like and explicitly cross-referenced to a previously reported UAP from the 48th Fighter Wing, suggesting a recognized recurring type.

quotes.text: LOOKS LIKE A BALLOON, SIMILAR TO PREVIOUSLY REPORTED UAP FROM 48FW.

key_findings.finding: The crew tracked the object as a 'weapons quality 1' track — the highest standard of tracking quality, sufficient for weapons employment — while it traveled with the winds at 31,000 feet MSL.

quotes.text: OBSERVED A WEAPONS QUALITY 1 TRACK  OF A UAP TRAVELING WITH THE WINDS AT 31,000 FT MSL IVO 323'S.

key_findings.finding: The crew generated a targeting solution ('next to shoot') on the UAP, indicating it was trackable enough for fire-control purposes.

quotes.text: WAS ABLE TO MAKE A NEXT TO SHOOT ON THE TRACK AND VISUALLY ID THE UAP IN THE TFLIR.

key_findings.finding: The UAP was visually confirmed using the aircraft's Targeting Forward Looking Infrared (TFLIR) sensor, making this both an infrared and visual-quality confirmation.

quotes.text: VISUALLY ID THE UAP IN THE TFLIR.

key_findings.finding: Five of the six pages are entirely withheld under FOIA exemption 1.4(a), meaning the operational details, crew identities, aircraft information, and likely imagery are classified and not disclosed in this release.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: This MISREP is the type of standardized military UAP report submitted to AARO, and the official description explicitly states military services use MISREPs to report UAP to AARO.

As a military aviation UAP report involving targeting sensors and tracking data, it feeds into the broader Air Force UAP reporting chain historically associated with Wright-Patterson, though no direct connection is stated.
